newsitem.title: USA: Wabash National Q1 backlog up vs year-end.
newsitem.headline: Wabash National Q1 backlog up vs year-end.

text.p: Wabash National Corp said Monday its backlog at the end of the first quarter was about $565 million, up more than $100 million from year-end levels.
The backlog represented net orders for the quarter of about $240 million, the highest level during the past two years, it added.

"Much of the order activity during the quarter involved our new proprietary composite plate trailer (the Duraplate trailer), which represents approximately $200 million of our total backlog," Jerry Ehrlich, chairman, said in a statement.
Wabash on Monday reported a drop in first quarter earnings to $0.05 a share from $0.12 a year ago.
In spite of the strong demand for the DuraPlate trailer, the continued limited supply of composite material restricted plate trailer production and revenues, he added.
Also impacting the first quarter were lost production days during January due to adverse weather conditions.
"Construction of the new composite material plant at our Lafayette facility remains on schedule with start-up expected during third quarter of 1997," Ehrlich said.
Wabash also has acquired certain assets from Fruehauf, including retail outlets in 31 major metropolitan markets.

"This acquisition represents a strategic fit in a number of areas, including new trailers (primarily refrigerated trailers, Fleet Flyer vans and dump trailers), used trailers and aftermarket parts," Ehrlich said. "It is anticipated this acquisition will be accretive to both cash flow and earnings this year."
